category: Killed / Injured — Plaine du Cul-de-Sac & Cité Soleil only (Mar 6 – Jul 31, 2026, UN)
note: The UN reported at least 613 people killed and 375 injured between March 6 and July 31, 2026 in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cité Soleil areas alone, with 18,000+ displaced from those two areas in the same period — cited in Haitian Times reporting (Aug 12, 2026) on renewed gang attacks in Arcahaie, Cité Soleil, and Kenscoff raising concerns over Dec. 13 election security.

OHCHR reported June 4, 2026: at least 2,310 killed, 1,100+ injured, 99 abductions, and sexual violence against approximately 699 women and girls from January 1 through June 4. Annualized pace: ~5,500–6,000 for full-year 2026. Q1 BINUH breakdown: security forces responsible for 69% of casualties (including 69 civilians/5 children in drone strikes); gangs directly responsible for 27%. Additional ~668 deaths from April 1–June 4 after Q1's 1,642 deaths reflects sustained high-tempo violence despite GSF launch and Village de Dieu offensive.

source: UN BINUH Q1 2026 Report, released May 8, 2026
note: UN BINUH Q1 2026 report documents at least 1,642 killed and 745 injured January–March 2026. Security forces responsible for 69% of casualties (including 69 civilians/5 children killed in drone strikes); gang members directly responsible for 27%. Violence spreading significantly beyond Port-au-Prince into Artibonite and Centre. Annualized pace projects 6,500+ for full-year 2026.

category: Civilian Deaths from Security Force Drone Strikes (Q1 2026)
source: UN BINUH Q1 2026 Report / UN News, May 8–10, 2026
note: BINUH Q1 2026 report confirmed 69 civilians including 5 children killed in security force drone strikes in Q1 2026. Security operations overall accounted for 69% of Q1 2026 deaths and injuries. HNP Task Force operates quadcopter drones with support from Vectus Global (US-licensed private military firm). HRW March 2026 report documented 1,243 people killed in 141 drone operations (Mar 2025–Jan 2026), including 17 children and 43 adults not believed to be gang members. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights said strikes are 'disproportionate and likely unlawful.'

source: UN BINUH Q1 2026 Report, May 8, 2026; PassBlue/UN May 21, 2026
note: BINUH Q1 2026 report documented 292 formally reported victims of sexual violence (Jan–Mar 2026), primarily girls and women aged 12–17 in gang-controlled zones, primarily gang rape. A separate PassBlue analysis (May 21, 2026) citing UN data estimated approximately 21 GBV cases per day in Q1 2026 — a 43% increase from Q4 2025 — with 70%+ involving rape. The 21/day figure (~1,890 for the quarter) reflects broader UN monitoring including unreported estimates, dwarfing the 292 formally documented cases. The gap illustrates the extreme underreporting of GBV in gang-controlled areas where victims face threats of retaliation, social stigma, and collapsed healthcare access. BINUH also documented the March 2026 execution of a 13-year-old gang 'lookout' killed for flying a kite.

Includes Cité Soleil massacre victims (207 confirmed). ACLED researchers note actual toll likely 70%+ higher due to underreporting in gang-held zones.

G9 vs. G-Pèp battle over Cité Soleil's Brooklyn quarter. 57 documented gang rapes. Snipers fired indiscriminately from rooftops. UN revised death toll upward from initial 47 to 207 confirmed in December 2024.

category: Cité Soleil / Croix-des-Bouquets Gang Clashes (May 9–14, 2026) — BINUH Provisional
source: UN BINUH provisional toll, May 14, 2026 / France 24 / Jamaica Observer
note: BINUH released a provisional toll May 14 confirming at least 78 killed and 66 wounded since May 9 in intra-Viv Ansanm gang clashes in Cité Soleil and Croix-des-Bouquets. At least 10 confirmed civilian deaths: 5 men, 4 women, 1 young girl. Broader context: 305 killed and 277 wounded in same two communes March 5–May 11, including 63 confirmed civilian residents (17 women, 13 children). Fighting pits Chen Mechan/Taliban/400 Mawozo vs. Duvivier/Pyè 6 factions over Cul-de-Sac Plain cargo route extortion. MSF Cité Soleil hospital (only facility for 300,000 residents) evacuated and closed since May 10. True toll expected significantly higher as gang-controlled zones prevent independent verification.

category: Cité Soleil / West Department Gang Violence (May 10–14, 2026)
source: HaitiLibre Zapping May 14, 2026 / IOM ETT #93 / OCHA Flash Update No. 1
note: HaitiLibre's May 14 Zapping roundup reported a cumulative toll of 80+ killed and 100+ wounded from the sustained gang warfare erupting across Cité Soleil, the Cul-de-Sac Plain (Croix-des-Missions, Canaan, Croix-des-Bouquets), and Martissant beginning May 10. This is significantly higher than initial AP wire reports focused only on the Cul-de-Sac sub-theater (8 killed). The fighting forced MSF to evacuate its Cité Soleil hospital — the only health facility for the commune's 300,000+ residents — after treating 40+ gunshot victims in 12 hours. Centre Hospitalier de Fontaine also suspended operations, evacuating 11 neonatal ICU newborns. Hundreds to ~5,000 displaced. IOM ETT #93 and OCHA Flash Update No. 1 issued formal humanitarian alerts. Hospital remained closed as of May 14. Affected areas under gang control of Viv Ansanm factions; fighting pitted Duvivier/Pyè 6 against Chen Mechan, Taliban, and 400 Mawozo over cargo route extortion revenues.

source: UN / BINUH / Al Jazeera / NPR / IOM DTM / Jamaica Gleaner, Aug 26-27, 2026
note: Viv Ansanm coalition gunmen (5 Segonn faction, led by Johnson "Izo 2" André) attacked Kenscoff on the night of August 23, 2026, torching roughly 25 homes and executing people inside a church sheltering earlier IDPs. The UN confirmed August 26 that the toll had risen to at least 47 killed, including 5+ children, and more than 50 kidnapped — one of Haiti's largest mass-kidnapping incidents in recent years. BINUH reported 22 victims were executed inside the church compound; RNDDH's independent count put the toll slightly lower at 45. IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix recorded 2,647 people (702 households) displaced Aug 23-25, mostly to host families in Pétion-Ville; two Kenscoff shelters closed. Toll marked "evolving" as initial Aug 24 reports cited 30 killed before the UN-confirmed Aug 26 revision to 47, and hostage estimates have ranged 50-60+ across outlets. Second major Kenscoff massacre in under two months, following the 61-killed attack of July 7-9, 2026. PNH opened a formal investigation Aug 24 into whether local police failure reflected complicity or negligence; by Aug 27 residents were demanding the local police chief's resignation and a gang leader was threatening to attack Tabarre (US embassy neighborhood) if security forces moved against the gang.

source: UN BINUH Q2 2026 Report / UN News, Aug 25, 2026
note: UN BINUH's Q2 2026 report documented 1,408 people killed and 656 injured between April and June 2026 — over 50% attributed directly to gangs, approximately 40% to security-force operations, and 5% to self-defense groups. At least 95 civilians were killed or injured during security-force operations, including 9 civilians (6 children) who died in explosive-drone strikes. BINUH separately documented at least 796 gang-related rape victims during the quarter, most involving multiple perpetrators. UN representative in Haiti Carlos Ruiz Massieu said "these figures show that the population continues to bear an unacceptable toll from violence." Nearly 1.47 million people were internally displaced as of May 2026, over half of them children.
